rationale: `mixes_in` for Zig is `usingnamespace`, which merges another struct's declaration SET into the enclosing container — member-set composition, with no conformance declared. It is rung R3: the pinned grammar already carries `using_namespace_declaration`, so nothing is patched and no node type is invented; the construct-site census over the whole admitted population (3,844 .zig files over 4 repositories, validation/m14/measurements/zig-extended-census.json) counts 0 sites, because the language removed the construct, so this fixture is the only place the emission can be observed. The rows pin the DIRECTION (composing container -> merged unit) and every argument form. The target is never the written PATH: the arbiter resolves target strings against SYMBOL NAMES, so a path target binds nothing while the stem does (the same measured rule the part-file lanes apply); the path survives as `meta.module` and the forbid rows make a regression to the path fail. A file-scope `usingnamespace` composes into the file's own unit, whose source is the lane's file-scope marker `(global)`. The import fact is untouched: the same statements still publish their imports/references rows, and this fixture does not restate them.

expectSymbols.name: merged
expectSymbols.note: the @import binding; a namespace import binding is a symbol (its alias names the module)

expectRelationships.note: POSITIVE 1 — the same-file struct form: the host's member set gains Shared's declarations.
POSITIVE 2 — the @import form: the target is the module's SYMBOL (the stem), and the written path stays in metadata.
POSITIVE 3 — the alias form: the merged unit is the binding the file published for the module.
POSITIVE 4 — `@import("x.zig").Member` composes the MEMBER's declaration set; the member is the target.
POSITIVE 5 — a file-scope `usingnamespace` composes into the file's own unit; the source is the lane's file-scope marker.

forbidRelationships.comment: the PATH is never the target: it binds nothing; the stem is the target and the path is metadata
same rule for the member form
same rule for the file-scope form
composition declares no conformance, so it is not an implements clause
there is no supertype here; a merged declaration set is not a base class
`usingnamespace` is a keyword-like declaration, not a callable; a calls edge to it would name a symbol that does not exist
